items.text: In the match between Gol Gohar Sirjan and Al Jazira in the AFC Champions League, the Syrian referee was replaced by the fourth official at halftime after controversial decisions and player protests. Gol Gohar's manager stated the referee was not in a normal state and the club warned that players would not return to the field if the referee was not replaced. The Asian Football Confederation has not yet provided an official explanation for the referee's replacement.

Fararu news agency reported that at the start of trading on Thursday, 5 Azar, the dollar rate reached 292,890. The price of the US dollar in Tehran's free market set a new record on Wednesday, 4 Azar, reaching 290,500 tomans in Tehran's Ferdowsi market.

Hamidreza Hajibabaei, the Deputy Speaker of the Parliament, stated that the only way to confront the US is "siege against siege" and threatened that if Iran's oil is not exported, no oil will leave the region. He added that if regional countries assist the US, the Islamic Republic will target the entire area. He also mentioned the possibility of changing the Islamic Republic's defense doctrine if necessary.

Islamabad hosts a meeting of senior political, defense, and military officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey to discuss practical steps for implementing the joint defense pact of Mecca. This meeting is held after the official enforcement of the pact and amid increasing concerns about regional threats. Javad Hamdani, a reporter from Iran International, reports.

Esteghlal team became the women's ice hockey premier league champion by defeating the Penguins 4-1, four weeks before the end of the competition. Yeganeh Bahrami leads the scorers table with 12 goals, and Hadiseh Pourhashami follows her teammate with 11 goals.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International saying that on 5 Azar, due to a power outage in Tehran, the elevator stopped and he has to wait about two hours until the power is restored.

Israel Katz, Israel's Defense Minister, announced that if Hamas does not disarm voluntarily, the Israeli army will launch a new military operation in the Gaza Strip. He said Hamas must disarm voluntarily or the Israeli army will do so. Katz added that Hamas's control over the remaining 30% of the Gaza Strip is an illusion and the army will continue efforts to end Hamas.

LeBron James, 41, shined with his first triple-double for the Philadelphia 76ers in the absence of key stars, scoring 25 points, 12 assists, and 10 rebounds in a 111-104 win over the Miami Heat. This was James's sixth triple-double after turning 40, a rare feat in NBA history. He had standout moments in the second and fourth quarters.

Houshang Hasenyari, an expert on Middle East and military affairs, said the Islamic Republic uses all available capacities to acquire unconventional weapons, including nuclear and chemical weapons. He stated that if the Islamic Republic obtains these weapons, given the regime's anti-Israeli policies, the possibility of using them against Israel can be considered.

Israeli media reported a tense phone call between Benjamin Netanyahu and Donald Trump regarding military action against the Islamic Republic. According to informed sources, Netanyahu tried to convince Trump to carry out a military attack in the near future during this call.

Mohammad Zouri, one of those arrested in connection with the protests of Dey 1404, remains in detention in Damghan prison without a clear status despite about six months having passed since his arrest.

Reza Shasipour was killed on 18 Dey during popular protests in the city of Izeh by direct gunfire from the Islamic Republic's suppression forces. His name remains in the memory of this land and his memory is a guiding light for freedom seekers.

A shopkeeper sent a video to Iran International saying that on the 5th of Azar, the electricity of a production workshop in Yaftabad, Tehran, was cut off from 9 AM and will not be restored until 12 PM. In reaction to this situation, he said: "I remember Khamenei's famous phrase that Islam is exactly this; not one word less, not one word more."

Hana Hattab, the Syrian referee of the Gol Gohar and Al Jazira match, reacted to accusations of alcohol consumption and his sudden substitution at halftime, threatening critics with official complaints and legal action. He expressed strong complaints about privacy invasion in a message on his personal page and stated that he will pursue any insults and defamation through judicial authorities. Hana Hattab also mentioned that before issuing an official statement about the AFC Champions League 2 events, he is waiting for the Syrian Football Federation's stance.

Mohammad Reza Aref, the First Vice President, expressed surprise at the increase in the price of macaroni and called for a reduction in prices. He said, "For once, make the people happy, lower the prices, and we will pray for you."

Citizens report to Iran International about the rise in the dollar price and inflation. They also complain about frequent unannounced power and gas outages and the worsening of daily life due to the energy crisis.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of the Iran International editorial team, referred to Naeem Qassem's statements about the Islamic Republic's financial support for Hezbollah and said Qassem speaks of continued Iranian financial aid while the Iranian people face an economic crisis. Akbarin emphasized that Qassem's claim that the Iranian people and officials believe they must bear the cost of supporting Hezbollah contradicts past years' protests by the Iranian people against the Islamic Republic's regional policies.

A labor activist of contract workers at Tehran's major electricity distribution company protested the low wages of contract workers, saying a significant part of their salaries decreases after deductions and their expertise allowance is not included in their payslips. He also said that official employees, despite doing similar work, earn almost twice as much and criticized the high income of contractors compared to the living conditions of the workers.

Joshua Kimmich criticized Bayern Munich's management sharply for pressuring Jamal Musiala after Bayern's defeat and expressed strong support for his ill teammate. Kimmich said the public handling of the issue is unacceptable and humanity should take precedence over club interests. Musiala suffers from a neurological disorder, and management's statements about reducing his salary have faced negative reactions.

Israel Hayom newspaper reported, quoting a Western diplomat, about decades-long efforts by the Islamic Republic to develop chemical weapons. Iran International also warned last year in an exclusive report about activities related to the development of chemical and biological warheads for ballistic missiles.

The Cultural Commission of the Parliament announced that the review of the "Regulation of widespread audio and video violations in cyberspace" bill has reached its final stages and will be referred to the Parliament's public session for review and approval after consolidation. This bill is designed to increase oversight of the production and dissemination of audio and video content in cyberspace. A member of the Cultural Commission said that the publication of content crossing "cultural and ethical red lines" was among the reasons for reviewing this bill.

Hossein Mohibi, spokesperson for the IRGC, said that missile production by the IRGC has not stopped and the status of missile reserves and offensive and defensive weaponry of the Islamic Republic is "much better than the United States." He added that the US is facing a shortage of strategic weapons, but the IRGC does not face shortages.

The UK Ministry of Defence has asked about 100,000 former military personnel to be ready to return to service in case of war. This action is the first since the end of the Cold War and follows increased concerns about military threats from Russia.
A video shows a group of students in Bojnord forming a circle, stamping their feet simultaneously, and singing the anthem "Eternal Name of the Homeland."

Tahir Naqvi, a lawyer serving his sentence in Evin Prison, has been banned from meeting his family. According to HRANA news agency, this ban was imposed as a punishment due to the publication of a letter.

The case of Raheem Sterling's dangerous driving and his admission to using nitrous oxide has revealed a hidden crisis in professional football. Sterling admitted to using this substance, and experts have warned about its widespread use. Doctors say this substance can destroy the sporting future and health of players.
The police commander of Mahallat reported the arrest of a citizen due to what was described as posting insulting content on social media.

Masoumeh Taherkhani, an economic analyst, said the upward trend of the dollar price continues and the dollar rate could reach 400,000 tomans by the end of the year. She also emphasized that power and gas outages in industries reduce production and supply and put employment at serious risk of workforce reduction and widespread layoffs.

Mojtaba Khamenei, leader of the Islamic Republic, stated in a written message on Basij Week that Basij members do not miss any opportunity to strike the enemies of Islam and the Islamic system. He said the Basij organization must experience a transformation and rebirth and form more advanced and new versions of Basij. He also emphasized that steps must be taken towards realizing the slogan "Every Iranian, a Basiji" and that Basij has compensated for many shortcomings of official and unofficial institutions.

Iman Aghayari, a political analyst, said the Islamic Republic faces a difficult situation in deciding on increasing transportation costs. According to him, whether the government agrees to this increase or prevents it, it will face irreparable consequences and increased public dissatisfaction.

A boy in Khoy has been deprived of a birth certificate for over seven months due to the Civil Registration Office's opposition to the chosen name "Alihan." The child was born on 21 Farvardin 1405 and still lacks a birth certificate. The Khoy Civil Registration Office has refused to issue a birth certificate for him.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International saying he paid 600,000 tomans for buying six bottles of mineral water, one juice, and two packs of wafers. He sarcastically referred to the high prices, saying: "One of the blessings of the Islamic Republic; we have come closer to the peak."

Turkey's Anka news agency reported, citing energy industry sources, that Iran and Turkey have agreed to extend their natural gas import contract for five years. The Turkish state company Botas and Iran Gas Company have agreed on the extension, and Botas has extended the license to import gas from Iran until April 18, 2032. According to the new agreement, Turkey will continue to import 10 billion cubic meters of natural gas annually from Iran, with no changes in the pricing formula or gas volume in the contract.

Farideh Hassanzadeh, public relations manager of Hormozgan University of Medical Sciences, announced that by 9 PM on Azar 4, 98 cases of poisoning were recorded in this province. Milad Taghdisi Heydarian, acting deputy of treatment at Nishapur University of Medical Sciences, announced that the number of people who visited medical centers in this city with symptoms of poisoning from alcohol consumption has reached 238, with five deaths and five cases of brain death reported so far.

A video sent to Iran International shows that a group of Iranians residing in Switzerland protested the flogging sentence of Parasto Ahmadi, a female singer, on December 4, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, by gathering in Zurich.

Amitis Ramazani, head of the Iranian Infectious Disease Specialists Association, announced that the spread of influenza has passed the warning threshold in most provinces of the country. She said the influenza wave started earlier this year than last year and the number of cases is increasing more rapidly. About 50% of positive influenza cases are seen in individuals under 15 years old, and children may suffer from more severe forms of the disease.

Jordan and the European Union, co-chairs of the Union for the Mediterranean meeting, called on all member countries of this union to join the "Cost-Free Passage through the Strait of Hormuz" pact. Foreign ministers of the Union for the Mediterranean member countries expressed support for the Gulf Cooperation Council members. They warned that instability in the region could disrupt the global supply chain of energy, fertilizers, and food for a long time.

German media report a possible separation of Manuel Neuer from his wife Annika just days after the birth of their second child. According to the German newspaper Bild, Neuer left his home after about three years of marriage and shortly after the birth of their second son in August, stating he does not wish to continue their life together. Annika Neuer reacted strongly on Instagram, saying that being a woman who was cheated on is not shameful, but it is shameful for a man to destroy his family and harm his wife and children emotionally and then blame others.

Ayoub Parkar, a 71-year-old political prisoner in Sheiban Prison in Ahvaz, despite having an infection at the hernia surgery site and severe pain, has been deprived of specialized medical care and re-referral to medical centers outside the prison. He was sent to the hospital for hernia surgery on 13 Mehr 1405 and developed an infection after returning to prison. Despite worsening pain, his medical care has been limited to oral medications and he has not been re-referred to the hospital.

Saud Abdulaziz Al-Otaibi, spokesperson for Kuwait's Ministry of Defense, announced that following an attack by the Islamic Republic on one of Kuwait's vital centers, four people including one Kuwaiti citizen, two Italian citizens, and one Pakistani citizen were injured. Kuwaiti armed forces identified and confronted hostile drones in Kuwaiti airspace. The injured were transferred to the hospital and material damages were also reported.

Videos show rough sea along the coastal roads of the San Francisco Bay area. Tall waves on Wednesday, 4 Azar, overflowed protective barriers and flooded streets. The US National Weather Service has issued a warning about coastal flooding and rising water levels.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, referred to Mojtaba Khamenei's message on the occasion of Basij Week, saying he emphasized the slogan "Every Iranian, a Basiji" while the participation of the IRGC and Basij in killing protesters has increased the distance of a large part of society from these two institutions. Kazemian said Khamenei's emphasis on using every opportunity to strike the "enemies of the regime" could mean a renewed emphasis on bloody suppression of protesters if protests return to the streets.

Emad Ghovidel, a protest rap singer, announced by posting an image of a judicial summons on his Instagram account that he has been summoned to the Fourth Investigative Branch of the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office in Rasht. According to this summons issued on the 1st of Azar 1405, Ghovidel must appear within five days to defend against the charge of "propaganda against the Islamic Republic system". Ghovidel also stated that since the beginning of this year, he has been interrogated six times, each time for six hours, and all his communication lines have been blocked for six months.

Israel Katz, Israel's defense minister, warned that if Hamas does not voluntarily disarm, the Israeli army will launch a large-scale military operation in the Gaza Strip. This operation will include displacing one million residents of Gaza to the south of the area. The warning comes as the White House and a peace delegation increase efforts to advance the reconstruction plan for Gaza, but the Israeli government insists on the complete disarmament of Hamas before starting this process.

Israel's Ministry of Defense announced that Israel and the United States evaluated about 20 advanced drone threat interception and countermeasure systems for the first time on Israeli soil in joint tests. These tests were conducted under the "Black Sands" program with participation from the US Central Command and Israeli military forces. The goal was to assess the efficiency of the systems and their suitability for operational needs under simulated threat conditions.

The Bangchak oil company in Thailand announced that following a fire on Thursday, 5 Azar, at the Bangkok oil refinery with a capacity of 120,000 barrels per day, all production units of this complex have been shut down. The fire was controlled about 30 minutes later. At least seven people, including four seriously, were injured.

Syrian anti-narcotics forces discovered about 2,300,000 Captagon pills in Tartus province and arrested two suspects. The Syrian General Directorate of Borders and Customs also seized a shipment of 783,000 Captagon pills that was to be smuggled from Lebanon.

The police commander of Khomam County reported the arrest of two suspects for animal abuse through organizing animal fights or forcing animals to fight each other in one of the villages of this county. According to him, the suspects were sent to prison by judicial order.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said that in the last decade of Bashar al-Assad's rule, 80% of the world's Captagon was produced in Syria, and the Fourth Armored Division of the Syrian army, commanded by Maher al-Assad, protected the factories and trafficking network. Akbarin added that the Secretary-General of Hezbollah in Lebanon supported the arrested traffickers, called them "our children," and demanded their swift release.

Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, striker of Deportivo La Coruña, had a car accident on the morning of Thursday, 4 Azar, on his way to training, with no injuries reported. The accident occurred at 9:23 AM on a highway in the La Coruña province, causing material damage to vehicles. Aubameyang is having an excellent season with his new team and is ready to face Barcelona.

A producer in Zanjan criticized the sharp increase in the cost of raw materials and tools in a video. He said he bought a container with about two liters of vinegar for 250,000 tomans, the price of cable rose from less than 100,000 tomans to over 230,000 tomans, and some items like spray, glue, and screws have also multiplied.

The Italian news agency ANSA and the newspaper La Repubblica reported that two Italian technicians of Rheinmetall were killed on Thursday, 5 Azar, due to the impact of debris from drones intercepted by the Islamic Republic at a vital facility in Kuwait. These two civilian technicians were deployed in Kuwait to operate the SkyNex air defense system. Additionally, a Kuwaiti citizen and a Pakistani citizen were injured in this attack.
A shopkeeper sent a video to Iran International showing the shops in Sanandaj market were dark, saying the electricity went out right at the busy hour of the market and disrupted business activities.

Jassim Al-Budaiwi, Secretary-General of the Gulf Cooperation Council, condemned the Islamic Republic's attack on a vital facility in Kuwait that resulted in the deaths of two Italian citizens and injuries to two others. He described the attacks as provocative and unjustifiable and held the Islamic Republic responsible for the consequences. Al-Budaiwi emphasized support for Kuwait's right to defend itself.

Milad Balsini, a Turkic activist, has been held in Tabriz prison without a judicial decision for over three months. His requests for temporary release have been rejected three times by the Tabriz prosecutor's office. He has not had access to a lawyer and his family has not been informed of the reasons for his detention.

Amirhadi Anvari from Iran International reports that the B-1 bridge on the northern ring road of Karaj, which connected the Garmdareh missile complexes to the headquarters of the 10th Seyyed al-Shohada Division of the IRGC, was targeted in an attack on 13 Farvardin during the second war. Additionally, three bridges on routes 32 and highway 2 were targeted on 14 and 18 Farvardin in the East Azerbaijan region.

The Telegram channel Khabaraneh reported that Mahdi Mahmoudian was severely beaten and tortured in the security police detention center after his arrest on Wednesday, 4 Azar, and was transferred to a hospital. Officers tried to force a confession by suffocating him with a plastic bag. Mahmoudian was transferred to Greater Tehran Prison after being charged with "propaganda against the regime" and "spreading lies."

Swedish police announced they will open their first foreign office in Iraq in early 2027 to pursue leaders of criminal networks and combat organized crime. This office will also cover Syria, Lebanon, and Jordan. Petra Lund, the head of Swedish police, said that arresting Rawa Majid, leader of the Fakstrat network, is important for Sweden but cooperation with Iran is not possible.
The head of the Social Work Department of the Deputy of Treatment at the Ministry of Health reported that more than 11,000 cases of child abuse occurred in the country over the past year.
A video received by Iran International shows that a citizen in Gachsaran wrote the slogan "Long live the Shah" on a street wall.

Chadormalu Ardakan drew 2-2 at home against Mes Shahr-e Babak in the 14th week of the Premier League. Reni Boboy and Aqil Anafche scored for Chadormalu, while Mes Shahr-e Babak equalized with goals from Homayoun Eftekhari and Aref Qezel. Aqil Anafche was sent off in the 55th minute, making conditions difficult for the home team.

Gideon Sa'ar, Israel's Foreign Minister, on Thursday, 5 Azar, reacted to the killing of two Italian citizens in a drone attack by the Islamic Republic on Kuwait, stating that the unchecked aggression of the Islamic Republic threatens the stability and security of the Middle East and beyond and must end. Sa'ar expressed sorrow over the death of the two Italian citizens on the social network X and emphasized Israel's solidarity with their families and the people of Italy.

Some viewers of Iran International reported in messages that despite the increase in tariffs, they still face slow and unstable internet. Some citizens also reported that after the 40-day war, their internet data packages run out unusually quickly.

A truck driver protested on social media about the sharp increase in costs and the mismatch between fares and wages with inflation. He said the cost of changing truck oil rose from 20 million to 67 million tomans, and the price of tires increased from 75 million to 210 million tomans, while drivers' fares only increased by 30 percent. He addressed the government spokesperson saying, "If you cannot, step aside so someone who can work comes."
Leaders of European Union member countries gathered in Brussels to discuss the EU budget, financing Ukraine in the war with Russia, and challenges in the Eurozone.

Mehdi Tartaar, Persepolis coach, criticized comparing opponents based on their table position and called to end controversies about his team's performance before the match against Aluminium Arak. He described Aluminium as a good team playing beautiful football and said his team is ready to earn three points. Tartaar also mentioned Esteghlal as a respected rival and said this league is unpredictable.

Ahmad Farhadpour, a political prisoner, remains detained in Sheiban Prison in Ahvaz despite the end of his sentence on 28 Aban 1405. His continued imprisonment is reported to be due to the opening of a new case against him in the Shush Prosecutor's Office. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.

The Canadian newspaper Globe and Mail reported that the sanctioned networks Press TV and RT, and the networks Al-Aqsa and Al-Manar, affiliated with Hamas and Hezbollah respectively, are accessible in Canada through unauthorized internet TV devices. The deputy leader of the Conservative Party accused the Canadian government of inaction in enforcing criminal laws, and the Canadian Broadcasters Association warned about the spread of misinformation. The Canadian Foreign Ministry stated that current sanctions do not prohibit online viewing of these networks.

The match between Besiktas of Turkey and Hapoel Be'er Sheva, representing Israel, in the Europa League was moved from Istanbul to a neutral ground in Batumi, Georgia due to security considerations. The game is scheduled for tonight and has faced adverse weather conditions before kickoff.

Abulfazl Shekarchi, senior spokesperson for the Islamic Republic's armed forces, denied Kuwait army's report about an attack by the Islamic Republic on one of Kuwait's vital facilities. He said no military or offensive operations were conducted by the Islamic Republic's armed forces in the region. Two Italian citizens died from injuries caused by a drone attack by the Islamic Republic on Kuwait, and one Kuwaiti and one Pakistani citizen were also injured.
In a received video, a citizen says that the sharp increase in the price of oil and tires has caused some trucks at the Khomeini terminal to refuse loading on the fifth of Azar.

Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Qatar, and Jordan separately condemned the drone attack by the Islamic Republic on a vital facility in Kuwait, which resulted in the death of two Italian citizens and the injury of two others. Saudi Arabia and Qatar warned that the continuation of these attacks would escalate tensions and instability in the region. Bahrain called on the UN Security Council to compel the Islamic Republic to stop the attacks and be held accountable.

By noon on Thursday, 5 Azar, the number of poisoned people in Hormozgan province reached 113, with seven deaths. In Nishapur, 230 people were poisoned, with five deaths and five cases of brain death recorded. Also, in Khoy county, 20 people were poisoned, with three deaths and seven people hospitalized in intensive care units.

The official Iraqi news agency reported on Thursday, 5 Azar, quoting a local source that Iraqi border forces have closed the Pashteh border crossing with Iran in Halabja province. The source said the order to close this crossing was issued from Baghdad and the border forces are only responsible for implementing this order.

Anthony Williams, a 33-year-old British man, was found guilty of 14 counts of attempted murder related to a knife attack on 10 people on a train to London last November at Cambridge Crown Court. Williams had previously admitted to 12 counts of grievous bodily harm and two counts of attempted grievous bodily harm but denied intent to kill. Psychiatrists said he suffered from acute psychosis caused by schizophrenia, and his sentence is likely to be issued in early 2027.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing a queue to buy motor oil in front of a distribution truck of Behran Oil Company products and said that the oil is distributed in a queue.

The former representative of workers at Iran Poplin Textile Company in Rasht reported the cancellation of his representation and his dismissal after pursuing workers' union demands. A social activist for Social Security retirees criticized delays in pension payments, retirees' medical problems, and the failure to implement the promised special wage increase for coal mine workers.
Due to lack of workplace safety and poor working conditions, two workers died in the cities of Isfahan and Ilam.

Antonio Tajani, Italy's Foreign Minister, announced that following the killing of two Italian citizens in a drone attack on Kuwait, his government will formally protest to the embassy of the Islamic Republic. Tajani also called on Tehran to exercise restraint and said there is no need to attack neighboring Arab countries of Iran that are not involved in the war.

Pirooz Ghorbani, head coach of Aluminium Arak, said he does not think about mid-table presence or player transfers at the end of the season, and all parts of the club must strive to form a winning mentality in the team. He added that there is still a big gap between his ideas and the team, and the goal is not only to transfer young players to bigger teams. Ghorbani also stated that changing the club's approach requires time, serious determination, and synergy, and he prefers to fight for victory with courage and offensive thinking.

Contrary to Iran's international commitments under the Convention on the Rights of the Child and obligations related to the non-use of children in military affairs, 590 students from the counties of Paveh, Marvdasht, and Bon were sent to operational areas in the south and west of the country.

The official Saudi Arabian news agency reported on Thursday, 5 Azar, quoting an official from the Ministry of Energy that the impact of an aerial projectile on the Jazan oil refinery caused a temporary halt to part of the refinery's operations, the death of a Nepali worker, and injuries to several other employees. According to the official, a fire broke out at the refinery following the attack, and emergency and technical teams immediately responded. The Saudi Ministry of Energy official stated that the injured in this attack are of various nationalities and are receiving medical care.

Tong Zhao, a senior researcher at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, said China's opposition to regime change through foreign intervention stems from Beijing's concern for its own political system's security. He added that China might not prevent US and Israeli efforts to change the regime in Iran, provided these efforts do not openly violate international law.

Elham Kholas Ardestani and Navid Tashakor, a Bahá'í couple living in Isfahan, were sentenced to prison by the judiciary. Navid Tashakor was sentenced to three years in prison and Elham Kholas Ardestani to 11 months in prison.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, denied Iran's involvement in the drone attack on Kuwait in a phone conversation with Jarrah Jabir Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, Kuwait's Foreign Minister. He also announced Iran's readiness to conduct joint investigations with Kuwait.

This article examines the legal responsibility of the Islamic Republic of Iran towards conscripted soldiers killed or injured in war and analyzes its foundations and limitations. It assumes that the state's responsibility has two layers: compensatory due to the compulsory nature of service and accountability related to fulfilling prevention and investigation obligations. The study is based on a descriptive-analytical research method and reviews domestic and international legal frameworks.

Benyamin Faraji, Iran's national table tennis player, and Alan Kormanglif from Kazakhstan won the bronze medal by reaching the semifinals of the World Junior Table Tennis Championships doubles competition. This pair lost 3-0 to the South Korean team in the semifinals and missed advancing to the final. Before that, they defeated the teams of India and Poland 3-2.

Mohammad Taheri-Parsa, a citizen from Sabzevar, is serving his prison sentence in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. He was previously sentenced to three years and six months in prison, with two years suspended and one year and two months to be served including detention time. He was transferred to Vakilabad Prison on 26 Aban.

A resident of Shahriar sent a video to Iran International showing four onions and a purchase receipt of 205,000 tomans, criticizing the high prices by saying: "We have not only reached the peaks, we have flown over them."
Fardad Farahzad reported in the audio version 24 that Netanyahu is pressuring Trump for an immediate attack on the Islamic Republic.

Mohammadreza Zanouzi, owner of Tractor club, acknowledged that choosing Oman as the host for the Asian competitions was his mistake and accepted responsibility for the team's results. He announced plans to strengthen the team in the mid-season and pursue legal actions regarding the Anzali incidents, and expressed dissatisfaction with Alireza Beiranvand's contractual statements. Zanouzi also mentioned travel difficulties in Asia and their impact on the team's performance.

The Israeli army announced on Thursday, 5 Azar, that it targeted dozens of rockets and launch pads in an airstrike on a training camp belonging to Hezbollah's Ridwan unit in the Ain al-Tineh area in southern Lebanon. The Israeli army emphasized that it will continue its operations to eliminate Hezbollah threats while adhering to the ceasefire agreement.

A citizen released a video showing extensive cutting of pine trees in a part of Shian Forest Park in Tehran on the fifth of Azar. Sawdust and signs of fire are also visible in the images. He protested this situation, saying parts of the forest have become empty.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said the killing of two Italian citizens in a drone attack by the Islamic Republic on a military base in Kuwait could affect the approach of European countries, especially Italy, towards the Islamic Republic. He emphasized that such attacks might become a factor in escalating conflicts and further expose the Gulf countries to insecurity.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said the Islamic Republic considers internal protests the main threat to its survival. The appointment of Hossein Taeb as head of Basij and emphasis on a "neighborhood-centered" approach indicate the government wants to contain protests before they spread citywide. Vaisi added that in case of another attack by the US and Israel, institutions involved in suppressing protests may be targeted more than before, and disruptions in fuel, electricity, and gas supply could weaken government control.

The Italian newspaper Corriere dello Sport reacted to the replacement of the Syrian referee in the Al Jazira UAE vs Gol Gohar Sirjan match in the AFC Champions League and reported allegations of intoxication against him. The referee made a mistake in the first half and was replaced after protests in the second half. The Asian Football Confederation has launched an investigation into the referee's condition, but the intoxication allegation has not been officially confirmed.

AC Milan defeated Olympiacos 4-2 in the fifth week of the Europa League. Milan was initially 2 goals behind but managed to score 4 goals and win. Milan's goals were scored by Omari Hutchinson, Alfa Sisse, Christian Pulisic, and Diego Moreira.

A video was released showing that well diggers in Damavand got trapped in a well due to a power outage and need to be rescued with ropes. The narrator of the video criticized the unplanned power cuts.

The match between Turkey's Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er Sheva in the Europa League was stopped for 30 minutes after Besiktas fans clashed with Georgian police and security forces used pepper spray. This happened after Palestinian flags were displayed and anti-Israel slogans were chanted. Besiktas eventually won 2-1.

Alireza Nourizadeh said the central government of Iraq is trying to increase its control over the oil lines of the Kurdistan Region amid growing pressure from the US and the expansion of oil smuggling to the Islamic Republic. He pointed to the disputes between Erbil and Sulaymaniyah and the influence of the Islamic Republic in Iraq and the Kurdistan Region, emphasizing that this situation is complex and not easily resolved.
Alireza Kiani addressed the hollow and superficial claims of the Islamic regime regarding military power and Iranian culture and traditions in episode 21 of the program "Fereydoun."

Iraqi border guards closed the Pushtah border crossing with Iran in Halabja province on Thursday, 5 Azar, by order of Baghdad. The Iraqi border commander announced the start of implementing the order to close all unofficial crossings with neighboring countries, including in the Kurdistan Region. This action follows the closure of the Chazabeh and Mandali-Sumar crossings in recent weeks.

Donald Trump said in a call with American soldiers on Thanksgiving that victory in Iran is within reach and will happen whenever he wants. He added they try to be lenient and provide opportunities for agreement but are not sure if the opportunity will be used. Trump also said many ask if Iranians are crazy and maybe they are.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said during a call with American soldiers on Thanksgiving that he considers Iranian officials to be crazy. He warned that if Iran acquires nuclear weapons, it might fire them at Israel and other Middle Eastern countries, causing a nuclear disaster. Trump also said Iran has the capability to reach Europe but not the US, and that is why they will not allow Iran to obtain nuclear weapons.

Donald Trump said in a conversation with American soldiers on Thanksgiving that the NATO Secretary General does not want the Islamic Republic to acquire nuclear weapons. Trump added that NATO has now deployed many forces in various regions. He also said that NATO is becoming much more involved in this issue than before.

Penny Wong, Australia's foreign minister, announced that the country sanctioned two individuals responsible for anti-Semitic attacks in Australia on Friday, who acted on behalf of the IRGC. Zuhair Hasib and Kazem Hamad organized the horrific 2024 anti-Semitic arson attacks against the Australian Jewish community using a complex chain of intermediaries. These attacks targeted the Louis Continental food complex in Sydney and a synagogue in Melbourne.

The Globe and Mail reported that networks such as Press TV, Al-Alam, and Al-Manar, affiliated with the Islamic Republic and Hezbollah, are broadcast in Canadian homes through illegal internet TV devices despite Canadian sanctions.
